query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating a controlled amount of silicon into the boride-based component will improve resistance to molten aluminum corrosion by promoting the in situ formation of a continuous Si-rich (SiO2) surface layer that passivates the substrate.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard boride-based component (without intentional silicon doping) used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
generation.intervention: Introduce silicon into the composition—targeting around 5 wt% silicon addition—either through alloying or a reactive surface treatment during processing.
generation.conditions: The intervention is expected to be effective under typical hot-dip aluminum plating conditions (e.g., molten aluminum at around 660°C) and up to moderately higher temperatures (approximately 700°C), where the formation and stability of the passivating film can be maintained.
generation.structural_mediator: The silicon is expected to oxidize at the surface during exposure, forming a continuous, adherent, Si-rich (likely SiO2-based) layer that acts as a barrier to molten aluminum penetration.
generation.mechanism: During immersion in molten aluminum, the presence of silicon promotes rapid oxidation forming a passivating SiO2-rich film. This film minimizes contact between the corrosive molten aluminum and the underlying boride matrix, thereby significantly reducing the rate of corrosion compared to the undoped baseline material.
generation.predicted_outcome: The silicon-doped boride-based components will exhibit a significantly lower rate of corrosion (evidenced by lower weight loss and reduced surface degradation) compared to undoped samples under identical hot-dip conditions.
generation.baseline: Undoped boride-based components exhibiting the standard corrosion rate when exposed to molten aluminum at plating conditions.
generation.boundary: The mechanism is expected to operate effectively only if the temperature does not exceed the stability range of the passivating film (roughly up to 700°C) and in environments where oxygen is sufficiently available to form the SiO2 layer. Excess silicon or processing variations might adversely affect the mechanical properties.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal silicon concentration and its uniform distribution remain to be fully determined; additionally, quantification of the improvement (e.g., percentage reduction in corrosion rate) requires experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of boride-based component samples: one set with a 5 wt% silicon incorporation and one undoped baseline. Expose both sets to molten aluminum under standardized hot-dip plating conditions (660°C) for an identical duration. After exposure, conduct a systematic analysis of weight loss, surface morphology (using scanning electron microscopy), and phase composition (via X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy) to assess the integrity and composition of the surface films.
measurements: Surface oxide layer thickness and continuity (via SEM)
Phase identification of the surface film (via XRD and EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the silicon-doped samples fail to show a statistically significant reduction in weight loss and surface corrosion compared to the undoped baseline, or if no continuous Si-rich passivating film is detected, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
